item.title: USC's latest terrible loss to Indiana Hoosiers might be the final straw for Lincoln Riley in LA
item.description: Jayden Maiava's red-zone interception and USC's five trips inside the Indiana 20 yielding just 13 points defined the crushing 27-13 collapse.
item.content:encoded:
Where have we ever seen this movie before? The USC Trojans, with their season and hopes of reaching the College Football Playoff on the line, on the road against another good team, needing to come through late in the fourth quarter to finally get the breakthrough win they need to reach the next level.

And they came up short.

While there's more to Saturday's 27-13 loss to the Indiana Hoosiers than any one play or incident, the embodiment of the Trojans' season, of head coach Lincoln Riley's tenure at USC, came halfway through the fourth quarter.

INDIANA HOOSIERS BOOST COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF HOPES WITH 27-13 WIN OVER USC TROJANS

Down 20-13, SC moved the ball down the field quickly, with Jayden Maiava completing a 34-yard pass to superstar freshman Trent Mosley to set up 1st-and-goal from the Hoosier's 8-yard-line. A quick two-yard run set up 2nd-and-goal from the six with 6:34 remaining. Maiava dropped back to pass and...telegraphed his intentions by staring down receiver Kayden Dixon-Wyatt, ignoring Indiana linebacker Isaiah Jones, and delivering a perfectly thrown and timed interception.

Just like that, a potential tie game became Indiana ball. And just as they so often have, the Trojans defense couldn't get the ball back with the game still in reach. The Hoosiers went 93 yards on just seven plays, with a 42-yard touchdown pass from Grant Wilson to Charlie Becker effectively ending the game. Though it was officially ended when Maiava threw yet another interception on SC's final drive of the game.

Again, to put the entire loss on that one play, 2nd-and-goal from the six, isn't doing SC's collapse enough justice. The Trojans dropped not one, not two, not three, but four interceptions. One thrown directly to a defense back that bounced off his chest. One that went through a defenders hands on a diving try in the end zone. One in which SC actually did catch the ball, miraculously, only to have it knocked away by the slightest bit of contact. And another just for fun.

They missed two field goals, a 51-yard try that hit off the upright, and, somehow, a 27-yard attempt that wasn't even close. To make matters worse, a random Indiana fan nailed a field goal from almost that exact same spot a few minutes later.

The missed attempt came after a 3rd-and-8 with an obvious pass interference on the Hoosiers incorrectly waved off because a linebacker got a fingertip the pass. Per NCAA rules, a tipped ball negates pass interference, but contact before the ball is touched should still be enforced. The contact on the play came before, and after, the tip, but the refs apparently determined otherwise. Though the fact it was even close points to Maiava's poor pass and decision making.

LINCOLN RILEY HAS CONFRONTATION WITH OHIO STATE AD, READS PREPARED STATEMENT TO MEDIA AFTER HUGE USC WIN

USC's two fourth quarter drives, pre-garbage time, resulted in 17 plays for 148 yards, both reaching to the Indiana 10-yard-line, and...zero points. Not three points, zero points. 148 yards on two drives, zero points. That wasn't an aberration; USC drove into the Indiana red zone five times throughout the game and scored just one touchdown. Five red zone opportunities, 13 total points.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

USC's defense was frequently in the right place at the right time, as evidenced by the four dropped interceptions, but they also gave up their share of trademark back-breaking mistakes too. With the game still tied late in the third quarter, Indiana had a 37-yard run, helped along by an obvious holding on No. 11 against a USC linebacker that wasn't called, that set the Hoosiers up for a go-ahead touchdown.

After Maiava's pick, SC needed a stop to get the ball back. Instead, the Hoosiers went four-yard run, five-yard run, eight-yard run, 12-yard run, two-yard run, five-yard-run, 42-yard touchdown pass. That was the fourth play of 30+ yards the SC defense gave up to an offense run by a backup quarterback.

It was a microcosm of the problems with the Lincoln Riley era in LA. Ten positives, outweighed by five negatives. A defense that isn't good to win games on their own. Missed opportunities on offense, particularly with short fields, missed field goals, and in the post Caleb Williams-era, quarterback play that simply isn't good enough. Especially on the road.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The loss was eerily reminiscent of the USC-Notre Dame game in 2025, when the Trojans took a 24-21 lead in the third quarter, then immediately gave up a 100-yard kickoff return. Still only down 27-24 after a missed PAT, Maiava threw yet another back breaking interception around midfield. The SC defense held, and the offense got the ball back, drove down to the Notre Dame 37-yard-line and...Makai Lemon fumbled on a trick play. The Irish scored on the ensuing drive, all but ending the game. Though Maiava added another late pick on the final drive of the game, just as he did against Indiana.

Much of the blame for Saturday's loss can be placed on the players; dropped picks aren't Riley's fault, and Maiava's interception was a textbook case of poor quarterback vision. But at some point, the blame has to come back on Riley, doesn't it?

This loss wouldn't have mattered as much if the Trojans had just beaten a very mediocre Wisconsin team on the road. They scored seven points and lost. Or if they'd have been able to hold serve against the Oregon Ducks playing backup QB Dylan Raiola for most of the game, at the LA Coliseum. They couldn't.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Maiava's played in a whopping 29 games for USC and Lincoln Riley now, and hasn't improved much. His footwork is awful, frequently unnecessarily throwing off his back foot. He often makes terrible decisions in pressure situations. His accuracy is atrocious as soon as there's pressure, and despite being a fairly mobile quarterback, he's all but stopped moving up in the pocket or running for free yards. That's a necessity in modern college football, and Maiava no longer even attempts it.

Some of that's on him, yes, but Riley's claim to fame is his work with quarterbacks. Why hasn't Maiava gotten better? Or why did he not evaluate Maiava's weaknesses and hit the transfer portal hard to find someone better?

We're somehow just two weeks removed from SC fans storming the field after a huge win over Ohio State, but with the Trojans once again out of the College Football Playoff, once again suffering a disastrous, self-inflicted loss on the road, once again staring down the barrel of a long offseason of wondering what went wrong, it's once again enough to start the "Lincoln Riley hot seat" conversations. Particularly considering RIley's dismissive pre-written statement after the Buckeyes' win implying that he always knew the Trojans would peak at the right time and get into the tournament.

Already, reports have suggested the Trojans could put his buyout together. And the crosstown rivalry game on Thanksgiving weekend might be the last try he has of staying in LA. UCLA in year one under Bob Chesney is a near-lock for the playoff, while Riley in year five is once again on the outside looking in. Lose to the Bruins, in a symbolic changing of the guard in LA, and it seems impossible that he's back at the Coliseum in 2027.

It's a roller coaster, and most of the SC fanbase is ready for it to end.

item.title: 'The Odyssey' actor John Leguizamo demands Democrats 'abolish ICE,' shut down detention centers
item.description: Actor John Leguizamo's Instagram video demands abolishing ICE, shutting down detention centers and ending the Electoral College in a sweeping policy list.
item.content:encoded:
"The Odyssey" actor John Leguizamo urged Democrats to abolish Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), shut down detention centers and protect abortion rights and transgender Americans on Friday, while outlining his priorities for the next Congress.

Leguizamo presented a lengthy list of demands in a video he posted on social media, along with an accompanying policy list aimed at lawmakers taking office in January. His immigration proposals also included protecting sanctuary cities, ending family separation and pursuing immigration reform.

"Alright, my project 2027, starting January 3rd: Get it done, Dems, all right? Guarantee affordable healthcare, Medicare for all, strengthen social security, abolish ICE, shut down detention centers, end family separation, immigration reform, protect sanctuary cities, comprehensive gun reform," he said in the video. 

JEFFRIES VOWS DEMOCRATS WON’T ‘GIVE A DIME’ TO TRUMP’S DEPORTATION EFFORTS

"Trial, and convict Stephen Miller for ICE murders, impeach Todd Blanche, end Citizens United, so there's no dark money in government," Leguizamo added. 

Leguizamo’s agenda also extended to changes in presidential powers, elections and the Supreme Court. He called for eliminating the Electoral College, limiting presidential pardon powers, ending presidential immunity and establishing term limits for Supreme Court justices. 

His economic priorities included a $20 federal minimum wage, a billionaire wealth tax, paid maternity leave and a 10% cap on credit card interest rates.

DEMOCRATS’ MIDTERM SWEEP OPENS PATH TO BYPASSING ELECTORAL COLLEGE BY 2028

The actor's demand to close detention centers overlaps with legislation already proposed by Democratic lawmakers, although Leguizamo's list did not provide the implementation details outlined in those bills.

Rep. Delia Ramirez, D-Ill., and Rep. Yvette Clarke, D-N.Y., introduced the Melt ICE Act in January. According to Ramirez’s office, it would remove immigration detention authorities from federal law and terminate existing detention contracts within two years of enactment. Her office outlined how the legislation would redirect the agency’s funding.

"Redirects ICE funding to community-based organizations to provide wrap-around services to communities around the country," her office said in its summary of the bill.

The proposal would also prohibit new detention contracts and require DHS to submit a plan to remove immigrants from ankle monitors within six months. Funding would instead go toward community services, including housing and health care.

'SQUAD' DEMOCRAT SLAMMED BY TRUMP ADMIN FOR MOST 'RADICAL' PLAN TARGETING ICE YET

Ramirez subsequently announced a broader proposal, the Reimagining Safety Act, to dismantle DHS and replace it with a Department of Community Safety.

Her office described a plan to abolish ICE and Customs and Border Protection while preserving customs functions and agencies responsible for disaster response, transportation security and cybersecurity.

Support for cutting ICE funding is not universal among Democrats. Rep. Henry Cuellar, D-Texas, previously opposed defunding.

"I don't believe in defunding ICE," Cuellar said, in a previous statement to Fox News Digital.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

In his post, the actor also called out former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif.; Rep. Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y.; and Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., while calling for new Democratic leadership. 

"My project 2027 starts Jan 3! If you have the cojones to sign on Dems and reps with wisdom. No more absences (means u Pelosi) no excuses! Enough is enough and if you can’t wrangle your peeps Hakeem then bye! ✌bye anyway you are compromised! And Schumer u too should go away! We need new leadership," the actor posted. 

Fox News Digital reached out to the offices of Pelosi, Jeffries, and Schumer for comment, but did not immediately hear back. 

Leguizamo’s latest demands followed an earlier appeal the actor made to his own audience. In January, he told followers who supported ICE to stop attending his performances and watching his films.

DEMS SEIZE ON MIDTERM ROUT TO DEMAND ICE REFORM, BUT POLLS REVEAL A TWIST IN WHO PRIORITIZED IMMIGRATION

"If you follow ICE, unfollow me, don’t come to my shows, and don’t watch my movies," Leguizamo said.

A DHS spokesperson told Fox News Digital that DHS law enforcement has been delivering on President Donald Trump's promises since day one. 

"Since Day One, DHS law enforcement has been delivering on President Trump’s promise to the American people to arrest and deport criminal illegal aliens including murderers, rapists, pedophiles, gang members, and terrorists," the spokesperson said. 

"Nearly 60% of ICE arrests are of illegal aliens charged or convicted of a crime in the U.S. More than three million illegal aliens are out of the country and counting. Our message is clear: if you come to our country illegally, we will find you, we will arrest you, and we will deport you," the spokesperson told Fox News Digital. 

The White House told Fox News Digital that Leguizamo was "out of touch" with Americans.

"This C-list Hollywood actor is out of touch with Americans. To most Americans, our brave ICE law enforcement officers are heroes who put their lives on the line to arrest murderers, rapists, pedophiles, terrorists, and gang members," White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis told Fox News Digital. 

"President Trump will never allow criminal illegal aliens to flood into our communities," Bis added.

item.title: Kris Statlander, Harley Cameron make AEW history as they capture women's tag team championship at Full Gear
item.description: Wrathlander captured the AEW Women's World Tag Team Championship at Full Gear after Kris Statlander hit Saturday Night Fever on Alex Windsor.
item.content:encoded:
All Elite Wrestling (AEW) may be a relatively young pro wrestling company in the greater landscape, but with a vast roster of wrestlers who bring different styles to the ring, history is bound to be made every now and again.

Kris Statlander and Harley Cameron did just that when the duo known as Wrathlander won the AEW Women’s World Tag Team Championship against Jamie Hayter and Alex Windsor at Full Gear on Saturday night.

Statlander was being put into a position for Windsor and Hayter’s finishing move. As Hayter bounced off the rope, Cameron tripped her up from outside the ring. Statlander turned the tables on Windsor and nailed Saturday Night Fever. She pinned Windsor for the win as Cameron held back Hayter.

It’s the first reign for Statlander and Cameron as a team. Statlander joined Willow Nightingale as the only AEW stars to hold the world title, TBS Championship and tag team title in their careers.

Cameron entered a league of her own.

She became the first woman to hold the tag team titles twice. She and Nightingale were the first-ever AEW women’s tag team champions. Now, she’s the only person to hold the belt twice.

Windsor and Hayter, known as The Brawling Birds, have their reign ended after 77 days. They knocked off Megan Bayne and Lena Kross, who were the champions for 168 days before losing to Windsor and Hayter at All In in August.

Wrathlander now stands alone as the champions and the AEW sickos will have to wait and see who will challenge them next.

item.title: Arizona State coach Kenny Dillingham drops diabolocial postgame quote after Sun Devils' road win at UCF
item.description: Kenny Dillingham's colorful postgame quote about excuses captured the moment after Arizona State's gritty 26-13 road win over UCF amid FAA chaos.
item.content:encoded:
Kenny Dillingham and his Arizona State Sun Devils thrived on what was a unique and incredibly chaotic college football Saturday.

Arizona State was among the many teams around the country that were affected by the nationwide ground stoppage issued by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) on Friday. While several teams opted to scrap their flight plans altogether and travel to their destination via bus, that wasn't exactly an option for the Sun Devils traveling cross-country from Tempe, Arizona, to Orlando, Florida, to take on UCF.

Ultimately, the contest was pushed back two hours from its originally scheduled time of 3:30 p.m. ET to give the Sun Devils more time to arrive on Saturday, and arrive they did. Arizona State jumped on a 6 a.m. flight on Saturday morning, took care of business, and left with a 26-13 victory.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Following his team's impressive road win, Dillingham gave some insight into his mindset given all the hurdles he and his team had to face, and did so with quite the epic saying involving a body part.

"Excuses are like buttholes; everybody has them, and they all stink, the head coach explained during his postgame press conference. "And that’s what tonight would have been. Like, it's just an excuse. At the end of the day you're going to take the field, for 60 minutes, and play a football game.

"You're either going to get it done or you're not. Nobody's going to care what the circumstance was, because nobody cares about circumstances; they care about results."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

While it may be a bit crass, Dillingham told no lies.

It would have been easy for the Sun Devils to show up lackadaisical, and even easier to lean on the built-in travel excuse if they hadn't pulled out the win on the road, but they didn't have to live in that reality after taking care of business against the Knights.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Arizona State's win in Orlando marked its first win away from home this season after losing on the road to Texas A&M, Texas Tech, and BYU earlier in the year.

Dillingham's group improved to 6-4 on the season with the win over UCF, with the most impressive stat line from the contest being the Sun Devils' defense holding the Knights to just 54 yards on the ground.

item.title: What Is a Prop Bet? Player Props, Team Props and Game Props Explained
item.description: A prop bet is a wager on something inside a game other than the final result, like a player's yards or the first touchdown scorer. Learn how props work and how they are priced.
item.content:encoded:
A prop bet is a wager on a specific statistic to happen in the event that doesn’t depend on who wins or loses the game. There are many types of prop markets, and the most common are in football. For example, you could wager on the running back’s rushing yards, or which team (and how) will score score first. Props are some of the most extensive games available in the market and they continue to expand with more options provided on every game. Prop bets are usually how most people build same-game parlays. 

A prop bet, short for proposition bet, is a wager on a specific outcome inside a game rather than on the final score. The team can lose, and your prop can still win. Sportsbooks post hundreds of props on a single NFL game and dozens on a regular season NBA or MLB game.

Props fall into three groups:

Most props are either over/under lines on a number or yes/no markets on an event. A few, like first touchdown scorer, list every eligible player at a different price.

A prop works like a small bet on a small game. The sportsbook projects a number, sets a line at or near it, and attaches a price to each side. You pick a side, and the result settles on the official box score.

The table explains why experienced bettors spend so much time on props. The lines are softer because the sportsbook cannot model every player in every game as carefully as it models the point spread. That cuts both ways: the book charges more juice to protect itself.

A player prop line starts with a projection. The sportsbook's model estimates the player's expected yards, points or receptions from recent usage, opponent, pace and game script. The line sits near the projection, usually at half point to avoid pushes. Both sides open around -115, and the book moves the line or the price as money comes in.

Payouts use standard American odds. At -115, you risk $115 to win $100. At +110, you risk $100 to win $110. The implied probability of -115 is about 53.5 percent, so the two sides of a prop together add up to about 107 percent. That extra 7 percent is the hold, and it is higher than the 4.5 percent hold on a standard -110 spread.

Most apps let you move a prop line up or down for a different price. Goff over 245.5 at -115 might become over 275.5 at +160 or over 215.5 at -200. Alternate lines turn one prop into a ladder of choices and feed most same game parlay builders.

The Super Bowl brings props on the coin toss, the length of the national anthem, the Gatorade color and the first song of the halftime show. Most state regulators allow only props tied to on field play, so the famous novelty markets are mostly a Nevada and offshore phenomenon. Legal apps in most states offer game and player props on the Super Bowl but not entertainment props.

Prop markets have drawn the most regulatory attention of any bet type, because a single player can influence a single stat more easily than a final score.

Prop is short for proposition. A prop bet is a wager on a specific event or statistic inside a game, such as a player's yards or the first team to score, rather than on the final result.

A player prop is a bet on one athlete's performance, usually as an over/under on a stat line like passing yards, points or strikeouts, or as a yes/no on an event like scoring a touchdown.

A prop bet is a single wager on one event. A parlay combines two or more bets into one ticket. Props are often used as the legs of a same game parlay.

At most sportsbooks the prop is voided and the stake is returned. If the player is active but records no stats, the prop usually stands as a loss on the over. Check the house rules.

Props have softer lines than spreads but carry more juice, usually -115 or worse on both sides. They reward bettors who follow usage and injuries closely and punish casual guesses.

It depends on the state. Ohio and Maryland prohibit props on individual college athletes, New Jersey blocks bets on in-state college teams, and Kentucky has no college restriction. College team props and game props remain available wherever college betting is legal.

Full game props include overtime unless the market name specifies a quarter or half. First half and quarter props end when that period ends.

item.title: What Is a Teaser Bet? How Teasers Work in Football and Basketball Betting
item.description: A teaser bet moves the point spread or total in your favor on two or more games. Learn how teasers work, what they pay and when a 6 point NFL teaser makes sense.
item.content:encoded:
A teaser bet is when you get to pair two or more plays and adjust the line in one way or another. Bettors use a teaser to give themselves a better price on a play without having to take as big of a risk on covering a spread or total. In exchange for being able to adjust the line, you are paying the book different prices. This will guide you through how to make a teaser bet and what things you should consider before placing the wager. 

Teasers are offered in football and basketball only, because those are the sports where points scored come in predictable chunks. You will not find a teaser on a baseball or hockey card.

A teaser bet is a type of parlay that lets you adjust the point spread or total on every leg by a fixed number of points. In football, the standard teaser is six points. In basketball, it is four. Every leg moves by the same amount and in your favor, and every leg has to win for the ticket to cash.

The trade-off is the price. A standard two-team point spread parlay pays about +260. A two-team six-point teaser pays somewhere between -110 and -120 depending on the sportsbook. You are paying for the points with the odds.

Teasers come in a few standard sizes:

Start with the standard lines, then move each one by the teaser amount in the direction that helps your side. Favorites get smaller, underdogs get bigger, overs get lower, and unders get higher.

Suppose you like two Sunday favorites, but both spreads feel like a touchdown too many. A two-team six-point teaser turns them into this:

Totals work the same way. A game total of 47.5 becomes 41.5 if you tease the over or 53.5 if you tease the under. You can mix spreads and totals on the same ticket, but most books will not let you tease both sides of the same game.

A teaser is a parlay with a discount on the lines and a discount on the payout. The question is which discount is bigger.


 

The parlay pays about three times as much, so the teaser only makes sense when the extra six points raise your win probability enough to cover that gap. In NFL betting that happens in one specific spot, covered below.

Unlike a standard parlay, a teaser payout is not calculated leg by leg. Each sportsbook publishes a fixed price for each number of legs at each teaser size. The table below shows the most common football prices. Books vary from 10 to 20 cents, so check the ticket before you confirm.

To work out a payout, treat the whole teaser as one bet at the listed price. A $50 three team six point teaser at +170 returns $85 in profit plus your $50 stake. A $50 two team teaser at -120 returns $41.67 in profit.

A teaser earns its price when the six points move a spread across the two most common NFL margins of victory: 3 and 7. Games are decided by exactly 3 points roughly 15 percent of the time and by exactly 7 points close to 9 percent of the time, so a line that starts on one side of those numbers and finishes on the other picks up a large share of outcomes.

Sportsbooks know this. Many now price two team teasers at -130 or -140, or shade the lines on exactly these games, which has thinned the edge. The logic still holds, but the margin is smaller than it was.

College spreads are larger and scores are more variable than in the NFL, so key numbers matter less. A six-point college teaser is usually a worse bet than the same teaser on an NFL card, even on a marquee SEC game.

Most sportsbooks price a two-team six-point football teaser between -110 and -120, so a $110 to $120 stake wins $100. Some books charge -130 or more, so always check the ticket.

A Wong teaser is a six-point NFL teaser that moves favorites of 7.5 to 8.5 down below 3, or underdogs of 1.5 to 2.5 up past 7. It is named for Stanford Wong, who showed these legs historically win often enough to beat the teaser price.

At most sportsbooks a push drops the teaser to the next lower number of legs. A two team teaser with one push becomes a single straight bet. Sweetheart teasers often count a push as a loss, so read the rules.

item.title: Where Is Sports Betting Legal? 2026 State-by-State Guide | OutKick
item.description: Sports betting is legal in 39 states plus DC, with online betting live in 31. Check the status, legal age and available sportsbooks in every state.
item.content:encoded:
Where is sports betting legal? As of November 2026, sports betting is legal in 39 states and Washington, DC, and online betting is live in 31 of those states plus DC. Eight states allow only in-person betting, and 11 have not legalized sports betting at all.

This guide covers the current status of every state, including launch dates, legal betting ages, college betting rules and which major sportsbooks operate where. It also tracks the states closest to legalizing next and explains how prediction markets fit into the picture.

Last updated: Nov. 12, 2026.

Sports betting falls into three categories across the US. Here is where every state stands as of November 2026.

Wisconsin is the closest to adding online betting. The state legalized tribal mobile betting in April 2026, but apps are not yet live.

For decades, the Professional and Amateur Sports Protection Act of 1992 (PASPA) barred most states from authorizing sports betting. Nevada was exempt. Delaware, Montana and Oregon kept limited carve-outs for older lottery-style products.

New Jersey challenged the law, and on May 14, 2018, the US Supreme Court ruled in Murphy v. NCAA that PASPA was unconstitutional. The decision left each state free to set its own rules, and Delaware took the first legal single-game bet outside Nevada weeks later.

Here is when each state took its first legal bet:

These 31 states and Washington, DC, allow online sports betting. Each listing covers the launch date, the state regulator, the minimum age, college betting rules and which of our featured sportsbooks are available.

Arizona launched online and retail betting on the same day in September 2021, timed to the start of the NFL season. It is one of the largest markets in the West, and all six of our featured sportsbooks operate there.

Arkansas opened casino sportsbooks in 2019 and added mobile betting in 2022, with the state's casinos running the apps. FanDuel entered in March 2026 as a partner of a casino licensee, which must keep at least 51% of the revenue.

Colorado voters approved sports betting through Proposition DD in 2019, and online and retail books opened in May 2020. It has one of the deepest app markets in the country.

Connecticut runs a three-operator market built on agreements with the Mashantucket Pequot and Mohegan tribes and the Connecticut Lottery. Only three operators are licensed online, including FanDuel and Fanatics.

Delaware took the first legal single-game sports bet outside Nevada on June 5, 2018. Online betting runs through a single lottery-contracted platform, so none of our featured sportsbooks operate there.

Florida's market is controlled by the Seminole Tribe under a 2021 gaming compact, which makes Hard Rock Bet the only legal online sportsbook in the state. After a federal court fight over the compact paused the 2021 launch, Hard Rock Bet relaunched statewide in late 2023.

Illinois is one of the largest markets in the country by handle. Since July 2025 operators have paid a per-wager tax on top of a graduated revenue tax, and Chicago began taxing sportsbook revenue in January 2026.

Indiana launched mobile betting in October 2019, one of the first states in the Midwest to do so. In September 2026 the Indiana Gaming Commission declined an NCAA request to ban college player props, leaving the question to lawmakers.

Iowa launched online and retail betting together in August 2019. In-person registration was required at first, but that rule ended in January 2021.

Kansas launched online betting in September 2022, with the Kansas Lottery as the operator of record. Current sportsbook contracts run through August 2027, and a 2025 budget provision barred the lottery from negotiating new ones, so the market's long-term structure is an open question.

Kentucky launched in September 2023 with an 18 and older minimum age. In April 2026 lawmakers overrode Gov. Andy Beshear's veto of HB 904, which raised the betting age to 21 effective July 15, 2026, and banned under-style player props on athletes at Kentucky colleges.

Louisiana legalized sports betting by parish-level vote in 2020, and online betting works only in the 55 of 64 parishes that approved it. The state raised its online tax rate to 21.5% in August 2025.

Online betting in Maine is reserved for the state's Wabanaki Nations, which partner with national operators. None of our featured sportsbooks operate there.

Maryland voters approved sports betting in 2020, and mobile apps launched just before Thanksgiving 2022. The state raised its online tax rate from 15% to 20% in 2025.

Massachusetts launched mobile betting in March 2023, just ahead of March Madness. Lawmakers have debated stricter rules, including limits on props and live betting, though none had become law as of October 2026.

Michigan launched online sports betting and online casino games on the same day in January 2021. bet365 became the latest major sportsbook to enter the state in April 2026.

Missouri voters approved Amendment 2 in November 2024, and online and retail betting launched together on December 1, 2025. It is the newest legal market in the country.

For a full breakdown of the state's legal sportsbooks, see our Missouri sports betting guide.

Nevada was the only state with full-scale legal sports betting before 2018, thanks to an exemption in federal law. Mobile apps are run by Nevada casino companies, and national brands such as FanDuel do not operate there.

New Hampshire runs a single-operator market through the state lottery, which keeps about half of the revenue, and none of our featured sportsbooks operate there. It is one of the few states where adults 18 and older can bet.

New Jersey brought the case that ended the federal ban, Murphy v. NCAA, and opened its first sportsbooks in June 2018. The state raised its online sports betting tax rate to 19.75% in 2025.

New York is the largest legal betting market in the country by handle, with mobile apps live since January 2022. Operators pay a 51% tax on online revenue, one of the highest rates in the country.

For a full breakdown of the state's legal sportsbooks, see our New York sports betting guide.

North Carolina launched mobile betting in March 2024, days before the ACC Tournament and March Madness. The state's July 2026 budget raised the online tax rate from 18% to 23%.

For a full breakdown of the state's legal sportsbooks, see our North Carolina sports betting guide.

Ohio launched online and retail betting together on January 1, 2023, during college football bowl season. A 2026 bill (HB 971) would sharply restrict online betting, but it had not advanced as of October 2026.

For a full breakdown of the state's legal sportsbooks, see our Ohio sports betting guide.

The Oregon Lottery runs the state's online market through a single-operator partnership, and no college betting is offered on the app. Tribal casinos offer in-person betting.

Pennsylvania legalized sports betting in 2017, before the federal ban was struck down, and launched online in May 2019. Its 36% tax rate on sportsbook revenue is among the highest in the country.

For a full breakdown of the state's legal sportsbooks, see our Pennsylvania sports betting guide.

The Rhode Island Lottery runs the state's only sportsbook, available in person and through a single statewide app. None of our featured sportsbooks operate there.

Tennessee was the first state to launch online-only betting with no retail sportsbooks. It taxes operators on the total amount wagered rather than revenue, which is unique among legal states.

Vermont launched online-only betting in January 2024 with three operators, including FanDuel and Fanatics.

Virginia launched mobile betting in January 2021, and casino sportsbooks followed in 2022. A 2026 law (HB 515) banned credit card deposits for sports betting starting July 1, 2026.

The District launched the lottery-run GambetDC app in 2020 and replaced it with FanDuel in 2024. A 2024 law change let private sportsbooks operate citywide, and bet365 became the latest to enter in September 2026.

West Virginia legalized sports betting before the Supreme Court ruling and opened its first sportsbook in August 2018. bet365 launched in the state in August 2026.

Wyoming offers online-only betting with no retail sportsbooks, and adults 18 and older can bet. The state places no cap on the number of sportsbook licenses.

These eight states allow sports betting only in person, usually at commercial or tribal casinos. Some offer apps, but they work only on casino property.

Mississippi opened casino sportsbooks in August 2018, and apps such as BetMGM work only on casino property. A bill to allow statewide mobile betting passed the House for a third straight year in 2026 but died in the Senate.

Montana's betting runs through the state lottery's Sports Bet Montana, available at licensed bars and taverns. The lottery app works only on those premises, so there is no statewide mobile betting.

Nebraska allows sports betting at its licensed racetrack casinos. Voters  decide don November 3, 2026, whether to legalize online sports betting through a constitutional amendment (Initiative Measure 440) and a companion statute. At the time of writing, it looks as if the vote will reject online sports betting.

New Mexico's tribal casinos began taking bets in October 2018 under existing gaming compacts, without new state legislation. Online betting is not available.

Sports betting in North Dakota is limited to a few tribal casinos. A 2025 proposal to put the question to voters failed, and the legislature does not meet again until 2027.

South Dakota voters approved betting in Deadwood casinos in 2020, and bets can be placed only in person or on casino property. A 2026 plan to put statewide mobile betting on the ballot died in a House committee.

Washington's tribal casinos offer sportsbooks and apps that work only on casino grounds. A 2026 law (SB 6137) began allowing bets on in-state college games while banning props on athletes at Washington schools.

Wisconsin legalized online betting through its tribes in April 2026, but apps have not launched because each tribal compact needs federal approval. A lawsuit filed in August 2026 challenges the law under the state constitution. 

Sports betting is not legal in 11 states. Here is where each one stands.

Alabama has no lottery or commercial casinos. A 2026 constitutional amendment covering a lottery, casinos and mobile betting died in committee, the third straight year a gambling bill failed.

Alaska has no legal sports betting. A mobile betting bill (HB 145) remains in committee and has never received a vote.

California voters rejected two sports betting measures in 2022, and no measure is on the 2026 ballot. Most observers point to 2028 as the next realistic attempt, which would likely need the support of the state's tribes.

A constitutional amendment fell short of the two-thirds House vote it needed in March 2026, and the companion framework bill never reached a floor vote. Georgia's next chance comes in the 2027 session.

Hawaii and Utah are the only states that ban all forms of gambling. Several 2026 bills stalled, and a state tourism and gaming working group is expected to report in late 2026 or early 2027.

Idaho's constitution limits gambling, and lawmakers have not seriously considered sports betting.

Minnesota has debated sports betting for years. A tribal-run mobile betting bill failed again in 2026 amid a long-running dispute between tribes and racetracks.

A bill to allow tribal retail and mobile betting failed in the state Senate in April 2026. Supporters plan to try again in 2027, when a new governor takes office.

A bill to create a state sports wagering commission received a hearing in February 2026 but did not advance.

Legalization requires a constitutional amendment approved by two-thirds of both chambers and then by voters. The legislature next meets in January 2027, and Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick remains opposed.

Utah's constitution bans all forms of gambling, and there is no effort to change it.

Several states have active legalization efforts heading into 2027. These are the ones to watch.

Not every sportsbook operates in every legal state. Here is where each of our featured sportsbooks is live online as of November 2026.

Florida is the only state where Hard Rock Bet is the sole legal online option. Delaware, Rhode Island and Nevada run their own state or casino-based platforms.

Prediction markets such as Kalshi and Polymarket let users trade contracts on the outcome of sporting events. They operate under federal oversight from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) rather than state gaming licenses, which is why they are available in some states where sportsbooks are not legal, including California and Texas.

Many states argue these contracts are sports betting and should require a state license. Federal appeals courts have split. The Third Circuit sided with Kalshi against New Jersey in April 2026, while the Ninth Circuit (Nevada, August 2026) and the Sixth Circuit (Ohio and Tennessee, September 2026) ruled that states can regulate sports event contracts. New Jersey has asked the US Supreme Court to take up the issue.

Prediction markets are not the same as a licensed sportsbook. They are not overseen by state gaming regulators, and state responsible gambling protections may not apply. FanDuel also runs a separate product, FanDuel Predicts, which offers sports contracts only in states where FanDuel Sportsbook is not available.

Offshore sportsbooks are not licensed or regulated by any US state. They often advertise to bettors in states without legal betting, but they offer no protection if a site refuses to pay, freezes an account or shuts down.

Licensed sportsbooks must verify your identity and location, keep player funds separate, follow state advertising rules and offer responsible gambling tools. If a sportsbook is not listed by your state regulator, it is not legal where you live.

The minimum age is 21 in most states. Adults 18 and older can bet in New Hampshire, Rhode Island, Wyoming, Montana and Washington DC, though some sportsbooks in DC, including BetMGM, set their own minimum of 21. In Washington, the age depends on the tribal casino. Kentucky raised its minimum age from 18 to 21 on July 15, 2026.

No. You only need to be physically located inside a legal state when you place a bet. Sportsbook apps use geolocation to confirm your location, so visitors can sign up and bet while they are in the state.

No. If you travel into a state without legal betting, your app will block wagers until you return to a legal state. You can usually still log in, view your account and withdraw funds.

Many states limit college betting. The most common rules ban bets on in-state college teams, ban player props on college athletes, or both. Restrictions are listed in each state's section above.

Sports betting should always be entertainment. If gambling stops being fun, these free and confidential resources can help.

Every legal sportsbook also offers deposit limits, time limits and self-exclusion tools, and most state regulators run their own self-exclusion programs.

Sports betting is legal in 39 states and Washington, DC, as of November 2026. Online betting is live in 31 of those states plus DC, while eight states allow only in-person betting.

Online betting is live in Arizona, Arkansas, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Florida, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Missouri, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Tennessee, Vermont, Virginia, West Virginia, Wyoming and Washington DC.

Sports betting is not legal in Alabama, Alaska, California, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Minnesota, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Texas and Utah.

The Supreme Court struck down the federal ban (PASPA) on May 14, 2018. Delaware took the first legal bet outside Nevada on June 5, 2018, and New Jersey followed days later.

The minimum age is 21 in most states. New Hampshire, Rhode Island, Wyoming, Montana and Washington DC allow betting at 18, though some sportsbooks set a higher minimum.

Yes. You do not need to be a resident. You only need to be physically located in a legal state when you place your bet.

Nebraska voters decided on online betting on November 3, 2026, and Wisconsin has legalized online betting but not yet launched. Texas, Georgia and Oklahoma are the largest states expected to revisit legalization in 2027.

Prediction markets operate under federal CFTC oversight rather than state gaming licenses, so they are not licensed sportsbooks. Several states are challenging them in court, and their legal status in some states remains unsettled.

item.title: Duffy: Investigators examining 2 routers after nationwide FAA ground stop, no signs of foreign cyberattack
item.description: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy says two routers from FAA facilities in Texas and Arkansas are undergoing deep diagnostics after the ground stop.
item.content:encoded:
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Sunday that two routers from FAA facilities in Texas and Arkansas are undergoing extensive testing as investigators examine whether faulty equipment or an installation problem triggered the nation's longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years.

Appearing on "Fox News Sunday," Duffy said that investigators have found no indication of a foreign cyberattack, although the FBI and other federal law enforcement partners remain involved in the probe.

"We think it was the installation or the router that was the bad actor," Duffy said. "But we're open, if we see something else, we're gonna continue to investigate with our federal partners and law enforcement."

FAA SAYS AIR TRAVEL SHOULD BE BACK TO NORMAL SUNDAY AFTER NATIONWIDE GROUND STOP

In an update posted on X, Duffy said contractor L3Harris had secured the two routers from remote FAA facilities in Texas and Arkansas and was conducting "deep diagnostics testing" at its headquarters in Florida, with engineers from the FAA, Juniper and Cisco assisting.

The investigation follows Friday's nationwide ground stop, which halted air traffic for more than four hours and contributed to disruptions affecting roughly 15,000 flights Friday and Saturday.

The fallout continued Sunday, with 3,798 flights delayed and another 1,638 canceled within, into or out of the United States as of noon ET, according to flight-tracking website FlightAware. Among the hardest-hit airports according to the provided data were Atlanta's Hartsfield-Jackson International Airport, with 376 delays, and Dallas Fort Worth International Airport, with 363 delays and 195 cancellations.

The shutdown occurred as L3Harris was replacing aging copper wiring with fiber-optic technology in the FAA's communications system. The work led to intermittent communications and radar gaps, prompting officials to halt flights nationwide.

Duffy said President Donald Trump convened federal officials on Friday as the administration investigated whether the disruption could have involved malicious interference.

"President Trump actually had the whole of government on the phone on Friday," Duffy said. "Was anyone seeing footprints? Was anyone hearing chatter? Was this a cyber attack from a foreign nation?"

"We have no indication that that was at play here," he added.

4 CRITICAL TRAVEL ISSUES FOR THOSE DELAYED AND DISRUPTED BY FAA NATIONWIDE GROUND STOP

Duffy defended the decision to issue the nationwide ground stop, emphasizing that passenger safety takes precedence when problems emerge in the FAA's communications network.

"When we have inconsistencies in our network we're going to shut it down," Duffy said.

The transportation secretary also warned that the FAA's communications infrastructure remains outdated despite ongoing efforts to replace copper wiring with fiber-optic technology.

"We're still using an old 1980 architecture for telecom," Duffy said. "I need a brand new telecom system."

BUTTIGIEG TAKES SWIPE AT TRUMP ADMINISTRATION AMID FAA FLIGHT CHAOS

Duffy said AT&T, Verizon and Lumen are prepared to help build a replacement network, but additional congressional funding is needed to move forward.

The request has drawn scrutiny from congressional Democrats, who argue the administration has yet to spend billions already allocated for air traffic control modernization. Duffy countered that the existing funds were designated for specific upgrades, including radar, radios and electronic flight strips, rather than a new communications network.

Meanwhile, FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said Saturday that "the worst is behind us," with air travel expected to return to normal by the end of Sunday.

The nationwide ground stop was the first since January 2023 and only the second since the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks.

Not only did Hammond complete the historic three-peat on Friday, but he also claimed the 2026 KBF Challenge Series Championship, earned Angler of the Year honors and set a new KBF record for the highest three-day total.

Not too shabby.

Hammond, who also won the 2025 Bassmaster Kayak Series National Championship, now has four national titles on his résumé. And his latest victory might have been his most impressive yet.

Hammond wasted no time getting to work at the KBF Championships on Lakes Guntersville and Wheeler.

He opened Wednesday's Challenge Series Championship with a 106-inch five-fish limit, building a commanding 9.75-inch lead over the rest of the field.

Watch Wyatt Hammond's full interview with OutKick OutDoors here:

For those unfamiliar with competitive kayak fishing, anglers are scored by the total length of their five longest bass rather than weight. Fish are measured, photographed and released instead of being transported to a traditional weigh-in.

On Thursday, Hammond followed up with another impressive limit of 102.25 inches, bringing his two-day total to 208.25 inches.

That was enough to win the Challenge Series Championship by a whopping 15.75 inches over runner-up Jody Queen.

But the biggest prize was still up for grabs.

FISHING IS BIG BUSINESS, AND FXR FOUNDER SAYS THE SPORT'S GROWTH IS ONLY GETTING STARTED

For Friday's KBF National Championship, the leaderboard reset to zero, meaning Hammond's massive lead from the previous two days meant absolutely nothing. He would have to do it all over again.

And that's exactly what he did.

Hammond landed another five-fish limit totaling 101.75 inches, narrowly edging out Rus Snyders, who finished with 100.50 inches. Abby Abbondanza took third with 99.25 inches.

Just 1.25 inches separated first and second place.

The victory made Hammond the first angler in KBF history to win three consecutive national championships.

And if that weren't enough, his combined total of 310 inches over the three days established a new KBF record. That's 15 scoring bass averaging more than 20 inches apiece.

What makes Hammond's latest accomplishment even more remarkable is what happened just a few weeks earlier.

In October, he came within two inches of defending his Bassmaster Kayak Series National Championship at Lake Murray in South Carolina.

Hammond told OutKick OutDoors that a slow start on Day 1 ultimately cost him, despite recording the largest single-day limit of the tournament on Day 2.

"I kind of got in my own head and kind of spun myself out," he explained.

But after settling down and sticking to his game plan, he finished strong. It just wasn't quite enough to catch eventual champion Ewing Minor.

During our conversation Wednesday, Hammond also opened up about the pressure that comes with being a national champion and how that pressure nearly burned him out on fishing altogether.

"I was really putting a lot of stress on myself. Like, I have to do well because, you know, I won a national championship," he said. "I have to continue doing well."

Eventually, Hammond realized he needed to stop worrying so much about the results and get back to enjoying the sport.

"I did a lot better whenever I enjoyed what I was doing," he said.

Judging by this week's results, that approach seems to be working out pretty well.

When I asked Hammond about his goals for 2027, he already had his sights set on another familiar rival.

"I'm gonna see if I can take something from Ewing [Minor] next year. I can't let him win everything all over again," he joked.

Hammond said winning Bassmaster's Angler of the Year award would be a dream, and he's particularly excited about upcoming tournaments at Lake Champlain and Sam Rayburn Reservoir.

But first, he can enjoy making history.

Three consecutive KBF national championships. Four national titles overall. A Challenge Series championship, an Angler of the Year award and a new KBF record.

Bravo, Wyatt.

item.title: Classic American pantry staples are getting a major protein- and fiber-packed makeover
item.description: Kraft Heinz CEO Steve Cahillane says brands were underinvested for over a decade as the company unveils protein Jell-O and cheesy ramen cups.
item.content:encoded:
Cheesy ramen, protein-packed Jell-O and round bacon slices specially cut for sandwiches are among the new twists coming to grocery stores as Kraft Heinz reportedly tries to breathe new life into old brands.

The new products, expected to hit shelves in the spring, are part of a broader push by the packaged-food giant to invest in innovation. They include Jell-O pudding with 10 grams of protein, Crystal Light with added fiber and protein, and Oscar Mayer Sandwich Bacon.

"It’s a big turnaround," Kraft Heinz CEO Steve Cahillane told the Wall Street Journal. "These brands have been underinvested in for over 10 years."

CAMPBELL'S ROLLS OUT NEW SOUPS, INCLUDING FIRST-EVER GLUTEN-FREE CHICKEN NOODLE VARIETY

Kraft Mac & Cheese Cheesy Ramen is set to arrive nationwide in early 2027, according to a press release. The instant noodle cups will come in Spicy, Chicken and Pork varieties and contain no artificial flavors, preservatives or dyes. Kraft said it is the brand’s first move into a new category in nearly 20 years and Cahillane said it sold out within a week of its Canadian launch.

The launch also follows the brand’s introduction of PowerMac, mac and cheese with added protein and fiber. Cahillane told the Journal that PowerMac helped return the brand to sales growth after several years.

AMERICA'S FAVORITE PIZZA MAY BE GETTING A MAKEOVER AS PROTEIN DEMAND SURGES

Kraft Heinz has invested an additional $700 million in its business, with funding for marketing, lower prices, staffing and product development. It also hired 400 employees, the outlet reported.

Its new offerings reflect consumers’ growing interest in protein and wellness, but the company is also staying true to its roots, focusing on taste and convenience.

WENDY'S BETS ON THICKER BACON, CREAMIER FROSTY IN BID TO REVERSE SALES SLUMP

About half of its 2027 product pipeline will focus on health and wellness, Cahillane told the Journal, including products with less sugar or more protein. But traditional Heinz ketchup will still be made with high-fructose corn syrup, he said, in part because cane sugar is more expensive.

"We’re not trying to claim that 100% of our portfolio is grown in your back garden," Cahillane said. "We are claiming that we can do health and wellness. We can play in that space, and we can do it extremely well."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

Oscar Mayer meat and Kraft cheese continue to struggle, according to Cahillane, as is Philadelphia cream cheese with consumers switching to cottage cheese. Kraft Heinz is trying to develop cream cheese products that rely less on carbohydrates like bagels.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Cahillane said he still expects sales to be flat next year, with sales and profits returning to growth in 2028. Kraft Heinz at one point planned to split into two companies, separating its global condiments business from its North American grocery unit, but Cahillane later paused the plan, telling the Journal that a split is no longer a focus.

But some analysts remain skeptical that the company’s struggling brands can be revived.

"There are too many holes in the boat, too many plates to spin," TD Cowen analyst Rob Moskow told the Journal. "I’m not sure how they can get it all done."

Part of the challenge is being in so many categories at the same time, Cahillane said: "We have to whack one mole at a time."

item.title: Former NHL player's monster catch inspires Missouri woman to reel in 1,200-pound sturgeon
item.description: Katharine Eckert's 11-foot, 4-inch white sturgeon from the Fraser River may be the largest freshwater fish ever caught by a woman, her guide says.
item.content:encoded:
Sometimes all it takes is a little inspiration from an NHL player to land the fish of a lifetime. Or, in Katharine Eckert's case, a fish that could weigh more than half a ton.

The Missouri woman decided to book a sturgeon fishing trip in British Columbia after reading about NHL defenseman Nick Leddy catching a monster fish with Canadian outfitter Sturgeon Slayers back in 2024. She figured it sounded like a pretty cool vacation activity.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

"I saw that article and thought, that would be really cool to do sometime," Eckert told FOX 2 in St. Louis. "Just something different to do on vacation rather than going to the beach or whatever."

What she didn't expect was to reel in an 11-foot, 4-inch white sturgeon estimated to weigh between 1,100 and 1,200 pounds— a catch her guide believes could be the largest freshwater fish ever caught by a woman.

Eckert, who lives in Maplewood, Mo., was fishing the Fraser River near Chilliwack, British Columbia, with her boyfriend, Justin, and Sturgeon Slayers founder Kevin Estrada when she hooked into the massive fish.

The ensuing battle lasted about 40 minutes.

"I remember thinking, 'My gosh, this is really hard,'" Eckert told FOX 2. "Once we got it closer to the boat, seeing it come out of the water a little bit, and realizing, 'Oh, we have something really incredible,' ... I was in shock, but also grateful for the experience."

According to Estrada, the sturgeon measured 60 inches around its body near the pectoral fins and a whopping 70 inches around its belly.

"Katharine's sturgeon was just as fat as the longer fish caught a week earlier by the men," Estrada told Wired2Fish, referring to another giant sturgeon his company had helped land.

That fish measured 11 feet, 8 inches and was also estimated at roughly 1,200 pounds.

Estrada said he hasn't been able to find a documented freshwater catch by a female angler that exceeds Eckert's fish. However, the potential world record comes with a caveat: The sturgeon was never officially weighed.

White sturgeon on British Columbia's Fraser River are protected under catch-and-release regulations, meaning anglers cannot keep them to put them on a certified scale. Instead, guides estimate their weight using measurements.

So while Eckert's catch is certainly a contender for the record books, it isn't an officially certified world record.

WORLD-RECORD BLUEFIN TUNA CAUGHT OFF THE COAST OF SAN DIEGO ON ROD AND REEL BY SPORT FISHERMAN

For Eckert, though, the experience was plenty rewarding without a certificate.

She grew up fishing for bass and catfish with her dad and has long been fascinated by sturgeon. In fact, she has a sturgeon tattoo and even named her dog Caviar.

Still, nothing quite prepared her for standing alongside one of these prehistoric giants.

"The pictures don't really do it justice," she told FOX 2. "Being in the presence of something that big in the moment is definitely something I'll never forget."

And the fish didn't just provide a great story and some incredible photos.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Eckert and the guides also helped collect valuable data for sturgeon conservation efforts. The fish was measured, tagged and safely released back into the Fraser River, where researchers can potentially track it in the future.

item.content:encoded:
Arch Manning was criticized, ripped, torched – whatever you want to call it – all over social media as he faced an uphill battle to get the Texas Longhorns back into the game against the LSU Tigers.

Manning powered through three interceptions to throw a game-winning touchdown pass to Raleek Brown, giving Texas a 22-21 win against LSU. It likely saved Texas’ chances at making the College Football Playoff, but it also put the final nail in the coffin for the Tigers’ hopes.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: AI mosquito trap targets deadly dengue outbreak
item.description: USF researchers built an AI mosquito trap with over 98% accuracy as Florida battles its largest dengue outbreak in decades with 524 local cases.
item.content:encoded:
You probably aren't thinking much about mosquitoes in November. In much of the country, cooler weather has sent those annoying little bloodsuckers into hiding. But in Florida, mosquitoes are still causing serious trouble. The state is dealing with its largest dengue outbreak in decades, and hundreds of people have caught the virus without leaving the state.

Now, researchers at the University of South Florida have developed an AI mosquito trap that could help health officials find dangerous mosquito species much faster. It can identify mosquito species with more than 98% accuracy in laboratory testing. And with dengue still spreading in Florida, the timing couldn't be more important.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

TROPICAL DISEASE SPREAD BY MOSQUITOES CLAIMS FIRST RECORDED DEATH IN SOUTHERN US STATE

If you thought mosquito season ended when summer did, Florida has a different story to tell. According to the Florida Department of Health's latest available weekly surveillance report, Hillsborough County has recorded 407 locally acquired dengue cases in 2026, the county's largest outbreak on record. Across Florida, health officials have reported 524 locally acquired cases through October 31. That means people contracted the virus from mosquitoes in the area rather than while traveling overseas.

The Tampa area has been hit especially hard. In October, the Florida Department of Health confirmed that Hillsborough County was still responding to an ongoing dengue outbreak. Dengue can cause high fever, severe headaches and intense muscle pain. In serious cases, it can lead to life-threatening complications. Health officials continue to encourage residents to take precautions against mosquito bites.

On November 13, Hillsborough County announced that it had extended its state of local emergency through November 19 as mosquito control crews increased aerial and ground treatments to help contain the outbreak. County officials say mosquito surveillance continues to detect dengue virus activity in neighborhoods across the area.

And here's why we're talking about this in November. While mosquitoes have largely disappeared from colder parts of the country, they can remain active in warmer states. Florida's outbreak shows that the threat doesn't disappear simply because summer is over. Meanwhile, a new generation of technology could give communities a better way to respond before mosquito populations get out of control.

The technology comes from Digitomy, a startup founded by researchers at the University of South Florida. Associate Professor Ryan Carney and Professor Sriram Chellappan have been developing the system through research dating back to 2018. Their goal is to help mosquito control teams identify the insects they're catching without spending days examining them under a microscope.

The trap itself looks fairly straightforward. Workers can hang it from a low tree branch or place it on the ground. A light or bait attracts mosquitoes, and a small fan pulls them inside. Once the insects land on a sticky pad, two built-in cameras photograph them. Artificial intelligence then compares those images against a large database to determine which mosquito species have been captured.

But the technology goes further. It can also identify whether a mosquito is male or female and whether it has recently fed on blood. That's useful information because female mosquitoes bite people and can transmit diseases. The researchers say their system achieved more than 98% accuracy in identifying mosquito species during laboratory testing.

GOOGLE WANTS TO RELEASE MILLIONS OF MOSQUITOES

Traditional mosquito surveillance can take two to three days because specialists often need to examine captured insects under a microscope. That's valuable work, but when health officials are trying to track a disease outbreak, waiting several days can slow their response. Digitomy wants to shorten that process dramatically. Its system uses AI and cloud computing with the goal of identifying captured mosquito species the same day. That could help mosquito control teams see where potentially dangerous species are appearing and decide where to concentrate their efforts.

This is especially important with Aedes aegypti, the mosquito species primarily responsible for spreading dengue in Florida. There are roughly 3,500 mosquito species worldwide, but only certain species spread particular diseases. Knowing which ones are present can help officials make better decisions. There's one important point to understand. The trap identifies mosquito species capable of carrying disease. It does not automatically prove that a captured mosquito is infected with dengue. Health officials would still need laboratory testing to confirm the presence of the virus.

What I find particularly interesting is what happens after the trap identifies a mosquito. Digitomy can send that information to a mapping dashboard, allowing mosquito control teams to see where certain species are appearing. The goal is to give mosquito control teams access to that information the same day, helping them identify where potentially dangerous species are appearing. Think about how useful that could be during an outbreak. If several traps begin detecting more Aedes aegypti mosquitoes in one neighborhood, officials could investigate that area and consider targeted mosquito control measures. Instead of waiting for more people to become sick, they could use surveillance data to guide their response.

The researchers have already integrated trap information into a private layer of their Global Mosquito Observations Dashboard at mosquitodashboard.org/. That system also incorporates more than half a million citizen science reports. The idea is to combine information from automated traps with observations from people who help track mosquitoes. Digitomy's technology could also complement an existing early warning system developed by Carney for dengue and West Nile virus. Together, these tools could give public health departments a clearer view of mosquito activity across communities. Of course, detecting mosquitoes early doesn't guarantee that an outbreak can be prevented. But faster information could help officials respond sooner, particularly in areas where mosquito control resources are limited.

Digitomy has already tested its technology at the University of South Florida and worked with the Anastasia Mosquito Control District in St. Johns County, which includes St. Augustine. The researchers are also preparing for field validation with Hillsborough County, where Florida's dengue outbreak has been especially severe. The startup is working with USF's Technology Transfer office to license the AI identification system to established mosquito trap manufacturers. That could allow companies to add the technology to equipment they already produce.

Digitomy is working toward commercial availability by licensing its AI technology to established mosquito trap manufacturers. For now, the university has not announced a consumer launch date or retail price. The company also received a $25,000 grant from the USF Research Foundation's Bull Ring Accelerator during summer 2026. The funding is intended to help accelerate the licensing and commercialization of university-developed technology. The team is also developing an online education platform that would allow mosquito control professionals and the public to practice identifying mosquito species using images and AI-generated feedback.

THIRD PERSON DIES AFTER MOSQUITO IS REPORTEDLY TRAPPED ON PLANE TO GERMANY IN 'AIRPORT MALARIA' PHENOMENON

You probably won't be hanging a Digitomy trap in your backyard anytime soon. But that doesn't mean this technology couldn't eventually affect your community. If mosquito control departments adopt smarter surveillance systems, they may be able to identify dangerous mosquito populations sooner and make better decisions about where to intervene. And even though we're heading into November, people living in warmer areas still need to pay attention to mosquito activity. If you're traveling to Florida or another place where mosquitoes remain active, taking precautions is important.

For now, the best protection is still fairly simple. Empty standing water from flowerpots and other outdoor containers because mosquitoes can breed in surprisingly small amounts of water. Use an EPA-registered insect repellent when spending time outdoors. Wearing long sleeves and pants can also help reduce exposed skin. We've covered some useful products that can help keep mosquitoes away, including repellents and outdoor gadgets.

You can find them in our guide to mosquito and tick repellents at CyberGuy.com

I think this is one of those uses of AI that could make a real difference in people's lives. Most of us see mosquitoes as an annoying part of summer. But Florida's dengue outbreak is a reminder that these tiny insects can cause serious health problems, even late in the year. What interests me about Digitomy is the possibility of giving mosquito control teams information while they still have time to act. The technology looks promising, especially with its reported accuracy in laboratory testing. But I want to see how it performs in real-world conditions before calling it a breakthrough. If it works as researchers hope, communities could have a valuable new tool to help protect people from mosquito-borne diseases. And that's a use of AI I can get behind.

item.title: Buttigieg takes swipe at Trump administration amid FAA flight chaos
item.description: Former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg joked he'd help travelers rebook flights at a hotel bar after the FAA's nationwide ground stop Friday.
item.content:encoded:
DENVER — Former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg took a swipe at the Trump administration’s handling of Friday’s nationwide FAA ground stop, joking that he would help stranded travelers rebook flights as delays and cancellations continued.

I’ll begin with a public service announcement," Buttigieg told reporters in Denver. "I will be available in the hotel bar following the concert for anybody who needs to rebook their flights or get a refund per your rights."

He made the remark as the "What’s Next" conference wrapped up in Denver. The two-day gathering, hosted by Majority Democrats, brought leaders together to discuss the party’s direction after its midterm victories.

DEMS DESCEND ON DENVER TO SIZE UP 2028; WE ASKED WHO WANTS IN THE RACE

The FAA lifted the ground stop shortly after 8 p.m. Friday, more than four hours after it began, but flights remained delayed and canceled over the weekend. The agency cited safety concerns and serious air traffic control communications issues.

Buttigieg, who said he had no inside information about the cause of the ground stop, later questioned why the aviation system’s safeguards had not prevented an outage of that scale. He said he was watching the disruption as a traveler with a flight scheduled for Saturday.

"The system has many redundancies in it, so that normally, if there’s one point of failure, something else can catch it," he said. "It is not clear to me why that redundancy did not prevent an outage of this magnitude."

SCHUMER'S LEADERSHIP RIVAL REVEALS MAJOR SENATE RULE CHANGE HE'D PURSUE IF ELECTED

Meanwhile, Trump administration officials offered a mixed account of the failure. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the cause remained under investigation, including whether a contractor made an error or equipment failed.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin later said the stoppage was not caused by artificial intelligence or a cyberattack, but by aging infrastructure that needs to be updated. President Donald Trump told Fox News that the system had broken down because of its age.

Friday’s disruption was the second nationwide ground stop since the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks. The first came in January 2023, when the FAA paused domestic departures for about 90 minutes because of an outage in its Notice to Air Missions system, which provides pilots with safety information.

The FAA said at the time it found no evidence of a cyberattack. Buttigieg ordered a review of that outage and directed the agency to report on what happened and recommend steps to prevent a recurrence.

item.title: Cruise passengers sharply divided over cutting buffet lines to sneak quick bites
item.description: Etiquette expert Diane Gottsman of Texas reveals why grabbing just one item while on a cruise ship buffet line still counts as cutting — and when rare exceptions apply.
item.content:encoded:
A common cruise ship buffet habit is raising questions — and eyebrows — about what passengers should and shouldn't do while filling their plates during meals.

Cutting ahead of others to grab just one item may seem a harmless action, but it can frustrate fellow passengers who have been patiently waiting their turn.

Buffet line-cutting was recently highlighted in a discussion about etiquette while at sea, according to the "Royal Caribbean Blog."

CRUISE BUFFET GUESTS FACE SURPRISE CHARGES FOR TAKING FOOD BACK TO CABINS

Passengers should wait their turn even if they only want something quick, such as a piece of toast or fruit, rather than squeezing past others or reaching around them, the blog advised.

Jumping ahead generally sends the wrong message, said Diane Gottsman, an etiquette expert based in Texas. 

"It's never acceptable to jump in front of someone in a buffet line, whether on a cruise ship, at a restaurant buffet or at a wedding," Gottsman said.

"Everyone is waiting their turn, so having someone jump in front of you comes across as rude," she added. "It also disrupts the flow of the buffet line, and in some cases can even cause a buffet traffic jam."

CRUISE PASSENGERS CRITICIZE NEW PROGRAM IDENTIFYING EARLY TIPPERS ON BOARD

There may be exceptions, however, depending on what someone needs and how crowded the buffet may be.

Gottsman said reaching in for a napkin is more understandable than cutting ahead to grab food. If only a few people are waiting, politely asking to step in briefly for a fork or knife may also be acceptable.

Holding a place for someone else can also test the patience of passengers who have been waiting.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"If you're holding a space for your spouse, a friend or a child, the child generally gets a pass," said Gottsman. But the spouse and friend are probably being judged and frustrating others who have been standing in line for 20 or 30 minutes."

If another passenger does cut the line, however, Gottsman generally advises against confronting the person over a minor offense.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

For someone who repeatedly jumps ahead, she suggested speaking with a manager in the dining area and allowing staff to handle the situation.

Cruise passengers themselves appear divided over exactly where to draw the line.

In a Reddit discussion, a traveler asked whether it was acceptable to skip ahead when people were waiting for the first dish at a buffet, but there was no line for other items farther down.

"If there's a wide opening, it's fine. If you're squeezing in between people, then go wait in line like everyone else," one person wrote.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Another commenter said the deciding factor should be whether the move holds up anyone already waiting.

"If they have to wait for you after getting [past] the first item, then you've cut in line," the user wrote.

"No, get in the line," another user chimed in.
